label: prf:frobenius-codim-universal
title: Proof of frobenius codim universal
html:
Proof. Since p_\lambda is central and primitive in Z(A), and each p_\lambda is \tau-dual to itself up to the scalar \tau(p_\lambda), linearity of \tau gives

  \tau(C_{\dim_q})
  \;=\;
  \sum_\lambda \frac{1}{\dim_q(\lambda) \cdot \tau(p_\lambda)}
    \cdot \tau(p_\lambda)
  \;=\;
  \sum_\lambda \frac{1}{\dim_q(\lambda)}.

\square

Uniqueness of C_{\dim_q} (categorical + forced).

Two answers. Uniqueness: the map Z(A) \ni z \mapsto \tau(z) \in \mathbb{C} is a linear functional on the centre. By non-degeneracy of \tau on Z(A) (which holds iff the Frobenius form restricts non-degenerately to the centre — true for any semisimple Frobenius algebra), the element z \in Z(A) with \tau(z) = \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q(\lambda) is unique. Writing z = \sum_\lambda c_\lambda p_\lambda and matching \tau(z) = \sum c_\lambda \cdot \tau(p_\lambda) to \sum 1/\dim_q forces c_\lambda = 1/(\dim_q(\lambda)\,\tau(p_\lambda)) — this is the definition of C_{\dim_q}. The element is therefore forced by the structure.

C_{\dim_q} is categorical in three distinct senses:

  1. The Frobenius pairing \tau \colon A \otimes A \to \mathbb{C} is a morphism in the monoidal category of A-bimodules; C_{\dim_q} is built from it by universal constructions (central idempotents + duality).
  2. The q-dimension \dim_q(\lambda) is the categorical quantum trace of the identity on the simple module V_\lambda — intrinsic to a ribbon-category / rigid-monoidal structure.
  3. In the equivalence between Frobenius algebras and 2D TQFTs (Atiyah–Segal / Abrams 1996 / Kock 2004 §2), every element of A corresponds to a decorated 2-cobordism. The standard Casimir \Omega = \sum e_i \cdot e^i corresponds to the torus with puncture; C_{\dim_q} corresponds to the torus with a \dim_q-labelled puncture, i.e., the torus twisted by the ribbon-category structure.

TQFT / handle-element interpretation. For a 2-dimensional TQFT with state-space A, the handle element of the torus-with-one-puncture is \mathrm{HE}_A := \sum_\lambda p_\lambda / \tau(p_\lambda) and its trace \tau(\mathrm{HE}_A) = \sum_\lambda d_\lambda (classical-dimension sum, e.g., the number of involutions for A = H_n(R, q)). The element C_{\dim_q} is the quantum refinement of the handle: an additional factor 1/\dim_q(\lambda) per block rescales by the block's quantum dimension rather than its classical one.

In Reshetikhin–Turaev language: if the MTC associated with A has S-matrix S_{\lambda\mu}, then \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = S_{\mathbf{1}, \mathbf{0}}^{-1} \cdot \sum_\lambda \dim_q(\lambda)^{-1} (modulo normalisation), which is a reciprocal of the global dimension weighted by self-duality.

Specialisations.

  1. A = H_n(R, q) with Markov trace \tau = \mathrm{tr}_M, \dim_q = q-hook-length dimension. \widehat{A} = \{\lambda \vdash n\}. Then \mathrm{tr}_M(C_{\dim_q}) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} 1/\dim_q(\lambda). At n = 3: = 2 + 1/[2]_q.
  2. A = Temperley–Lieb \mathrm{TL}_n(q) with Markov trace. \widehat{A} = \{\text{Jones–Wenzl idempotents}\}. The co-Casimir trace is a q-weighted sum over Jones–Wenzl blocks.
  3. A = group algebra \mathbb{C}[G] with \tau = uniform (Haar) trace. \dim_q = \dim (classical). Then \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = \sum_\lambda 1/\dim(\lambda), the reciprocal-dimension character sum — a known group-theoretic invariant related to the number of conjugacy classes via the first-orthogonality identity.

GB-filtration (confinement) decomposition. When A = H_n(R, q) is filtered by the confinement filtration J^\bullet(q) (confinement level), the partitions \lambda sort by level \ell(\lambda) = \mathrm{height}(\lambda) - 1. The Frobenius co-Casimir trace decomposes

  \tau(C_{\dim_q})
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\ell = 0}^{n-1} \;
    \sum_{\lambda :\; \ell(\lambda) = \ell}
      \frac{1}{\dim_q(\lambda)},

with the self-dual pairing under Young-diagram transpose (\lambda \leftrightarrow \lambda') identifying level \ell with level n - 1 - \ell. Each self-dual pair contributes an equal 1/\dim_q value (since \dim_q(\lambda) = \dim_q(\lambda') for any q). At the extremes \ell = 0 and \ell = n-1:

  \dim_q\bigl((n)\bigr) \;=\; 1 \;=\; \dim_q\bigl((1^n)\bigr),

so levels 0 and n-1 contribute exactly 1 each, giving the universal bound

  \tau(C_{\dim_q}) \;\geq\; 2 \qquad \text{for all } n \geq 1.

Middle levels carry all the q-dependence. For n = 3 only one middle level exists (level 1, \lambda = (2,1)), giving \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = 2 + 1/[2]_q.

Independence of the vortex \varrho. \tau(C_{\dim_q}^{(A)}) is independent of the specific vortex \varrho — it depends only on the algebra A (equivalently on n and q), not on the braid word \sigma_w representing \varrho. This is both a feature and a limitation:

  • Feature (universality): Every vortex on H_3(R, q) — proton (uud), neutron (udd), any nucleon-like trefoil — inherits the same (2 + 1/[2]_q) \cdot m_e additive offset. Mass differences between nucleons come entirely from the descended |\mathrm{tr}_M| and brane-tower pieces, not from the Frobenius correction.
  • Limitation (vortex-blind): The Frobenius correction cannot by itself distinguish \varrho_{\mathfrak{p}} from \varrho_{\mathfrak{n}} or any other trefoil-like vortex. Vortex-dependent corrections — e.g. chirality factors \{1+h, 1-h^2, (1-h^2)^2\} per (figure-eight BW coefficients) or knot-factor Frobenius pairings per (knot-factor Frobenius pairing) — are separate structural terms beyond \tau(C_{\dim_q}).

The unified mass formula (unified knot mass) therefore has three tiers:

  1. Vortex-specific: descended |\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_w)| and brane tower \sum \Phi_q.
  2. Algebra-specific (but vortex-independent): Frobenius co-Casimir \tau(C_{\dim_q}^{(A)}).
  3. Isotope-specific (vortex-dependent but structural): chirality / knot-factor coefficients from thm:six-term-mass-formula-complete.

Consistency.

  1. At q = 1 (classical limit): \dim_q \to d_\lambda and \tau(p_\lambda) \to d_\lambda/|G| (group-algebra trace), so C_{\dim_q} reduces to \sum_\lambda |G|/d_\lambda^2 \cdot p_\lambda and its trace is \sum_\lambda 1/d_\lambda — the classical reciprocal-dimension sum.
  2. In the "single-vortex" case A = H_3(R, q), three blocks \{(3), (2,1), (1,1,1)\} with q-dims \{1, [2]_q, 1\} give \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = 2 + 1/[2]_q matching proton residual to 0.14\% at q_0 \approx 1.11.
  3. The self-duality \lambda \leftrightarrow \lambda' is the categorical shadow of the Young-diagram transpose symmetry of the Hecke algebra, which in turn descends from the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1}) \sigma_i + 1 admitting two eigenvalues (q, -q^{-1}) — the source of all q-deformation structure in the paper.

Explicit Lean closures by partition count n

For each n, the Frobenius co-Casimir trace \tau(C_{\dim_q}^{(n)}) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} 1/\dim_q(\lambda) admits an explicit closed form via \mathrm{Fin}\,p(n) enumeration once a Lean definition of \dim_q(\lambda) for each partition is available. The convention used throughout is the quantum hook-length formula \dim_q(\lambda) = [n]_q!\,/\,\prod_{x \in \lambda} [h_x]_q, which reduces to the classical S_n-irrep dimension at q = 1.

The status table:

n p(n) conj. pairs self-conj. Lean theorem nucleus covered
3 3 1 1 ((2,1)) inline at \sigma_w-trace \mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{n} (single-vortex)
6 11 5 1 ((3,2,1)) hecke_n6_frobenius_codim {}^{4}He (H_{12} block; )
7 15 7 1 ((4,2,1)) hecke_n7_frobenius_codim A \ge 5 nuclei
8 22 10 2 ((4,2,1,1), (3,3,2)) hecke_n8_frobenius_codim {}^4He / {}^{16}O / {}^{20}Ne

Each closure follows the same proof scheme: (i) a Fin.sum_univ_* decomposition lemma extending Mathlib's Fin.sum_univ_eight to p(n) summands via a sequence of Fin.sum_univ_castSucc peels; (ii) per-partition @[simp] lemmas unfolding \dim_q(\lambda) to its product-of-q-integers form; (iii) the trace identity itself, discharged by simp + ring after the conjugate-pair grouping.

The n = 8 closure introduces partitions whose hook-product cancellation against [8]_q! leaves residual /[2]_q factors (specifically (5,1,1,1), (4,4), (4,1,1,1,1), (2,2,2,2)). These are encoded as (q + q^{-1})^{-1} in the explicit dim_q expressions; the ring discharge handles them via real-arithmetic field identities. Self-conjugates at n = 8 are (4,2,1,1) and (3,3,2). The complete index map and the conjugate-symmetric Fin 22 ordering are documented in frobenius-codim-universal.lean.

The generator that produces the per-partition \dim_q table and the Lean source is the canonical formalism; the JSON output and per-partition factor signatures are committed under phase5-n8-dim-q-table.json.

Beyond n = 8, the same scheme extends mechanically to n = 9 (partitions of 9, p(9) = 30, needed for triton and {}^{3}He at H_9) and n = 12 (p(12) = 77, needed for {}^{4}He's H_{12} substrate when not yet decomposed). The bottleneck above n = 8 is the size of the explicit \dim_q table rather than the proof scheme; both can be machine-generated by extending the the formal derivation formalism.
